## What's new in 0.3.0
Campertron now has a web UI. Start the console with `--web` and you can set up notifications, edit your searches and settings, search, look up campgrounds and run the monitoring from a browser on your home network, with a guided setup for a first start. This version also changes how the monitoring treats cancellations: a campsite night you were told about is reported again once Campertron has seen it booked and then open again. The desktop app makes better use of a large window and can send a test email or notification.

Your settings, search files, campground list and `Camp.History` work as they are and need no changes. Read "Upgrading from 0.2.0" below before you upgrade a computer or container that monitors.

### The web UI
- **Start it** with `CampertronConsole --web` (on Windows `CampertronConsole.exe --web`) from the console download, or with `--web` in the container. It is opt-in: without `--web`, the console and the container start as before.
- **Where it listens:** port 8790 on every network interface, so other devices on your home network can open it. `--listen 127.0.0.1` keeps it to the computer it runs on, and `--port` chooses another port.
- **A password is on by default.** The first start writes a one-time setup code to the console (in Docker, to `docker logs`). Enter it in the browser and choose a password of 10 to 128 characters before anything else opens. The code works once, for 30 minutes; only a hash of the password is kept, in `Web.password` in the settings folder.
- **Guided setup:** when nothing is set up yet, you land on four steps after signing in: choose email or ntfy, enter its settings and send a test, create a first search, and turn the monitoring on. Each step saves the same files as the full pages, so you can leave and come back; **Skip guided setup** leads to the full web UI.
- **The full web UI** has the desktop app's features and checks: **Searches** (create and edit search files, with the campground picker and the filter lists), **Results** (run the searches you select now, with booking links), **Settings** (`General.yaml`, `Email.yaml`, `Ntfy.yaml`, `Web.yaml`, and **System** with the current configuration, a refresh of the campground data and the **System**, **Light** or **Dark** theme, which each browser keeps for itself) and **Campgrounds** (look up by park, city or state).
- **Monitoring:** whether the monitoring runs, why it stopped, the last and the next check and the last check's new openings, with **Start**, **Stop** and **Restart**. When `outputTo` is `Email` or `Ntfy` and your settings are complete, web mode starts the monitoring by itself, and it keeps running when you sign out or close the page.
- **Pages that follow what is running:** while a search, a refresh of the campground data or the monitoring runs, its page updates by itself, in place, without reloading or losing your place. The pages also work without JavaScript and on a phone's screen.
- The [web UI guide](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/blob/master/docs/web-ui.md) covers the command line, the password and sessions, every page, `Web.yaml`, reverse proxies and the health check.

### Test messages, a random ntfy topic and `Web.yaml` in both apps
- **Send a test email** and **Send a test notification**, in the desktop app, the web UI and the guided setup, send one message with your saved settings and say whether the server accepted it. They read the password or token only for that message, work whatever `outputTo` is, and record nothing.
- **Generate a random topic** fills in a long random ntfy topic, in both apps. It is saved only when you save; then subscribe to the new topic in the ntfy app.
- `Web.yaml`, the web UI's settings file, can be edited under **Settings** in the desktop app as well as in the web UI.

### The desktop app
- **It uses the space of a large window.** In a wide or maximized window each tab takes the width that helps it: **Results** spreads its results across the window, **Searches** and a campground's details use up to two columns, and **Settings** and **System** stay at a readable width in the middle. A narrow window shows one column. Maximize and resize as you like: what you entered and selected stays.
- Everything else works as before: the **Searches**, **Results**, **Settings** and **Campgrounds** tabs, the themes, the current configuration and the refresh of the campground data. It runs searches only when you ask, and doesn't monitor.

### Notifications after cancellations
- **Reported again after it reopens.** An opening is reported once and not again while it stays available, also after a restart. Once a completed check sees that campsite night booked or otherwise unavailable, Campertron forgets it, so if it opens up again, for example after another cancellation, you are notified again. Before, an opening was never reported again.
- **Only what the checks see:** a night that is booked and freed again between two checks, or in a month no search checks, looks continuously available and isn't reported again.
- **Stays of several nights in a row** (`consecutiveDays`) are reported whole when any of their nights is new. Before, a night that had been reported was left out before the stays were put together, so a new, longer stay that included it, or a stay whose middle night was booked and freed again, could be missed for good.
- **One monitoring for a settings folder:** a second console, container or web UI on the same folder refuses to start its monitoring, so you never get every notification twice. Searching now isn't affected.
- **Unchanged:** an opening is recorded only after a notification about it was delivered. If a notification can't be sent, the monitoring stops after that check with an error, and what it couldn't deliver is reported again at the next start. Searching now (**Results** and the console's **Search**) sends nothing and neither reads nor changes `Camp.History`.

### Security and backups
- **The web UI is made for a home network you trust.** It speaks plain HTTP: anyone who can watch your network traffic can read the password and the session, and a password doesn't make it safe on the Internet, so don't forward a router port to it. For HTTPS, put it behind a reverse proxy you run, list the proxy in `trustedProxies` and its host name in `allowedHosts` in `Web.yaml`, and keep the web UI itself off the network; Campertron has no HTTPS server of its own.
- **Its protections:** it answers only to its own host names, accepts changes only from its own pages, limits sign-in attempts and other actions, tells browsers not to frame it or load anything from elsewhere, keeps its error pages to fixed wording, and reads forwarded headers only from the proxies you list. Sessions live in web mode's memory and end when you sign out, after 8 hours without use, after 7 days, or when web mode restarts. Turning the password off (`passwordProtection: false`) lets everyone who can reach the web UI change your settings.
- **Secrets stay out of the pages:** the web UI never shows the SMTP password (its box is write-only), says only yes or no for `CAMPERTRON_EMAIL_PASSWORD` and `CAMPERTRON_NTFY_TOKEN`, and checks the password and token files without opening them. The ntfy topic appears only in the `Ntfy.yaml` form: keep it private, because on a server without access control anyone who knows it can read your notifications.
- **Backups without old secrets:** saving a settings file still keeps the previous version as `.bak`. When a save replaces or removes the plain-text SMTP password in `Email.yaml`, or the topic in `Ntfy.yaml`, the backup now leaves that value empty and keeps the other previous settings. Campertron never reads or restores a backup; if you copy one back by hand, enter the password or topic again.

> **Old backups can still hold old secrets.** An `Email.yaml.bak` or `Ntfy.yaml.bak` saved by version 0.2.0 or earlier can still contain a plain-text SMTP password or an ntfy topic you have since replaced or removed. Campertron doesn't clean these up when it starts. Saving `Email.yaml` or `Ntfy.yaml` once with this version replaces its backup; if you don't need a backup, you can delete it. Deleting or replacing a file doesn't securely erase it from the disk.

### Running in Docker
- **The web UI in a container:** add `--web` and publish port 8790 (or `127.0.0.1:8790:8790` to keep it to the computer Docker runs on), then read the setup code with `docker logs`. Without `--web` the container monitors as before.
- **Mount `/config` and `/cache`:** `/config` holds your settings, searches, `Camp.History` and the campground list (back it up); a refresh of the campground data now downloads into `/cache` and needs about 1.15 GB free there while it runs.
- **Health check:** `/healthz` answers `ok` without a password, and `CampertronConsole --healthcheck` asks it (the README's Docker Compose example uses it). It shows only that the web UI answers, not whether the monitoring runs; the image itself has no health check.
- The image is now based on the ASP.NET Core runtime and is larger. Don't run a web UI container and a monitoring container on the same `/config` at once: only one of them can monitor it.

### Other improvements
- One app icon for the desktop app's program and window, the console's Windows program and the web UI's browser tab.
- Before publishing, the release workflow now also starts web mode from the released console downloads and in both container images, and checks its health check, its refusal of foreign requests, its setup page and its clean stop.

## Upgrading from 0.2.0
1. **Back up your settings folder** (`CampertronConfig`, or the folder you mount as `/config`). With Docker, keep the same `/cache` mount.
2. **Stop 0.2.0's monitoring** (its console or container) before you start this version: 0.2.0 doesn't take the new monitoring lock, so both could monitor the same folder.
3. **Desktop and console:** extract the new archives and use them instead of your old Campertron folders. **Docker:** use this version's image tag (see "Docker" below) and recreate the container with the same `/config` and `/cache` mounts; add `--web` and publish port 8790 only if you want the web UI.
4. **Nothing to edit:** your settings files, search files, campground list and `Camp.History` work as they are. The upgrade needs no refresh of the campground data; the list you have stays.
5. **Openings 0.2.0 reported** count as reported. Each is reported again once this version has seen it unavailable and then open again.
6. **New files** appear in the settings folder: `Campertron.monitoring.lock`, and once you use the web UI, `Web.password`, the `Web.keys` folder and, if you save its settings, `Web.yaml`. Keep the folder private.
7. **Check your old backups** (see "Old backups can still hold old secrets" above).

## Going back to 0.2.0
- Move `Web.yaml` out of the settings folder first, if you saved one: 0.2.0 takes it for a search file. The other new files can stay.
- 0.2.0 doesn't take the monitoring lock, so don't run it beside this version on the same settings folder.
- With Docker, use the image tag `0.2.0` or `0.2`, not `latest`.
- 0.2.0 reads what this version recorded in `Camp.History` and goes back to never reporting a recorded opening again, also after a cancellation.

## Upgrading from an earlier version
Follow the steps above, and read the upgrade notes of the versions in between: the [0.2.0 notes](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/releases/tag/v0.2.0) and the notes they point to.

## How this version was checked
- Every change passed the automated build and tests, now with tests of the web UI's pages, request checks, accessibility and self-updating pages, and a scan for known vulnerable packages.
- Before publishing, the downloads and both container images are started as the table under "Downloads" below shows, and the console's now also in web mode. These checks show that the programs start, answer and stop; they don't sign in, search or send notifications there.
- The tests met email, ntfy and recreation.gov only as local stand-ins; no real server was contacted by them.

## Known limitations
- **No HTTPS of its own, one password:** the web UI speaks plain HTTP (use your own reverse proxy for HTTPS) and has one password; several users and an installable web app aren't supported.
- **The desktop app** has no guided setup and doesn't monitor.
- **Browsers and platforms:** the web UI's own tests run on Linux, and its browser tests use headless Chrome only (not Firefox, Safari or a screen reader); on Windows and macOS the release checks only start it and check its answers. The desktop app's new layout was looked at on Linux only.
- **Only a status of exactly `Available` counts,** and Campertron doesn't count the places left at a site several groups can book.
- **A page left open doesn't keep you signed in:** after 8 hours without use you sign in again, and a search still running then ends with the session.
- **A refresh of the campground data** needs about 1.15 GB of free disk space while it runs, and Campertron doesn't check the free space first. After a refresh in the web UI, restart web mode so every page uses the new data. A refresh started in the desktop app or the console doesn't pause the web UI's monitoring.
- **Searching one campground for the first time in two Campertron programs at once** can make one of the searches stop with an error; run it again.
- **Email and ntfy are the only notifications;** other services, such as webhooks, Gotify, Discord, Telegram or Pushover, aren't supported.
- **No installers or macOS app bundle:** the programs are plain executables, aren't code-signed, and the macOS programs aren't notarized.
- **The included campground list is recreation.gov's data of November 10, 2026.** Refresh it to see campsites added since.
- Avalonia, the desktop app's UI framework, supports 32-bit Windows (`win-x86`) commercially only and doesn't list 32-bit ARM Linux desktops (`linux-arm`).

## Questions and problems
Found a bug, or something doesn't work as described? [Open an issue](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/issues) with the output of `CampertronConsole --version`, your operating system, which app you used and what happened. Don't post your `Email.yaml`, `Ntfy.yaml` or their backups, your password or token files, `Web.password`, the `Web.keys` folder or a setup code, and remove passwords, tokens, topics and email addresses from anything you share.

Campertron is not affiliated with or endorsed by Recreation.gov. It finds openings; you book them on recreation.gov.
